key_facts: Devon's third quarter results were outstanding, showcasing the power of its Delaware focused asset portfolio and the benefits of its financially driven business model.

Devon's team's focus on operations excellence has established impressive momentum, allowing the company to capture efficiencies, accelerate free cash flow, reduce leverage, and return a market-leading amount of cash to shareholders.
Devon's 2022 upstream capital program is directionally planned to be in the range of $1.9 billion to $2.2 billion, with a WTI breakeven price of around $30.
Devon's free cash flow is expected to grow by more than 40% compared to 2021, with an 18% free cash flow yield at an $80 WTI price.
Devon has authorized a $1 billion share repurchase program through year-end 2022, equivalent to approximately 4% of its current market capitalization.
Devon's implied dividend yield in 2022 is more than double that of the energy sector and more than seven times higher than the average company in the S&P 500 Index.
Devon's Delaware Basin assets account for roughly 80% of its capital deployment, with 13 operated rigs and four frac crews running during the quarter.
Devon's third quarter average D&C costs improved to $554 per lateral foot, a 41% decrease from a few years ago.
Devon has a concentrated 300,000 net acre position in the liquids-rich window of the Anadarko Basin, with a joint venture agreement with Dow providing drilling carry.
Devon's financial strategy includes a fixed plus variable dividend framework, with the board approving a 71% increase in dividend payout to $0.84 per share for the quarter.
Devon has retired over $1.2 billion of outstanding notes and built a $2.3 billion cash balance at quarter end, reaching a debt-to-EBITDA leverage target of one turn or less.
Devon's free cash flow yield is expected to strengthen in 2022, with the company on pace to nearly double its dividend next year.
Devon's financial strategy includes a focus on reducing debt and improving the balance sheet, with plans to retire approximately $1.0 billion of low-premium debt in 2022 and 2023.
Devon's third quarter operating cash flow totaled $1.6 billion, an increase of 46% compared to last quarter, and generated $1.1 billion of free cash flow, the highest amount ever in a single quarter.

Devon's financial strategy includes a share buyback program, which will be executed opportunistically when equity trades at a discounted valuation to historical multiples and in multiple levels of its highest quality peers.
Devon's capital allocation process is rigorous, with a focus on the competitiveness of investment mix and a detailed subsurface evaluation across its portfolio.
Devon has a deep inventory of opportunities concentrated in the best U.S. resource plays, with more than a decade of low-risk and high-return inventory in the Delaware Basin.
Devon's financial strategy includes a focus on achieving short-term, midterm, and long-term ESG targets, with a laser focus on meeting the needs of investors, the market, and society.
